details.alignment: Lawful Neutral (protective, oath-bound, suspicious of betrayal)

biography.value:
Toad Lee — Warden of the Toads

Level 4 Barbarian; Liberated Toads, The Wardens. Toad Lee was freed from the Vigilance trafficking barrels and became one of the people who made survival into an organized duty. He is not a decorative hero: he assigns a guard, spots routes, carries an axe, and asks what happens after the door opens.

Operational record

Lee helped hold the line against the Coat, organized fractured survivors with Speaker L, pursued Waluigi during the Lounge Brawl with deliberately nonlethal leg-targeting swings, and kept functioning after Stucky's thrown eye landed on his head. He is the brain of the Feywild operation when the plan needs a roof, a route, or a fallback.

Sheet boundary

This is a level 4 playable translation of the lore. It includes confirmed themes—axe work, Rage, Warden discipline, pursuit, and survivor logistics—without inventing legendary loot or high-level magic. The XP ledger remains authoritative: 5,790 XP, 3 AP spent, 0 available.

details.appearance: A compact, hardy Toad carrying an axe too large for anyone who has not watched him use it. Scarred by flight, imprisonment, and the work of keeping frightened people alive.
details.trait: I inventory exits, rooftops, and who is standing between the vulnerable and the door.
details.ideal: Protection is an action, not a speech. No Toad is cargo.
details.bond: The Wardens and the Liberated Toads; Speaker L; every survivor who needs a line held.
details.flaw: I make plans inside plans and can mistake vigilance for certainty.
details.eyes: Two ordinary eyes and one Feyward sensory eye
details.faith: Unresolved; has encountered forces that call themselves gods
details.skin: Toad green with Feywild color shift

languages.custom: Toad dialect; Liberated Toads field signs; Legion procedural terminology learned in captivity.

armorProf.custom: Light, medium, and heavy armor; shields. Dan fights one-handed and does not receive a second-weapon benefit.

weaponProf.custom: Simple and martial weapons; longsword; one-handed use only.

biography.value:
Feyward Dan — Player Character Dossier

Level 3 One-Armed Feyward Paladin / Dimensional Escapee. This is the parallel Feyward Dan, not the original Dan who led the Liberated Toads and lost his arm to the corrupted mage staff. Feyward Dan woke in a yellow bed at Prismari's school, survived goblin betrayal, escaped through a window, was dragged through the Mazebound, slept through multiple dimensional emergencies, and opened his third sensory eye during the Imp Ambush.

Ledger: 1,960 XP, 11 entries, Level 3, Power 5 Mortal. The actor is a playable translation of the lore; the XP ledger remains authoritative.

Confirmed carried inventory: one sword of uncertain provenance, chain mail, Shield +1, Holy Symbol of Ravenkind, and ten gold pieces. The sword is the blade Dan used when he charged Professor Prismari after the explosion on Estragon's Island. The school journal, Prismari, Mazebound, and other events remain in the biography and source records rather than being invented as carried loot.

Inventory rule: this actor deliberately contains only gear and abilities Dan actually has or was explicitly assigned. Memories, event records, and things he merely saw are not added to the inventory as fake loot.

How to play Feyward Dan

Use charm, improvisation, and sensory magic before force. Dan is not a polished wizard. He is a displaced player character who survives by testing doors, apologizing, fleeing when necessary, and returning when the party needs his eye.

One-armed paladin rules

Dan uses a longsword in his remaining hand and a shield in the other available hand. He cannot dual-wield or make two-handed weapon attacks. Divine Sense, Divine Smite, and the Aura of Life campaign item are included as documents. Aura of Life is recorded as a story/boon item and should be level-gated by the GM if standard 5e progression is being enforced.
biography.public: Feyward Dan is a parallel Toad with a colorful Feywild aura, an unreliable itinerary, and one extra eye that sees what invisible enemies hoped would remain unseen.

description.value: Rage-fueled protector trained by necessity. Hit Die d12; Rage 3/long rest; Danger Sense; Reckless Attack; Ability Score Improvement at level 4.
Small amphibious survivor. Advantage on checks to navigate familiar sewer, marsh, and rooftop routes; can squeeze through spaces sized for Small creatures.
You were treated as cargo and now organize people so it cannot happen again. Proficiencies: Survival and Investigation; Liberated Toads contacts.
Bonus Action; 3/Long Rest. For 1 minute, gain resistance to bludgeoning, piercing, and slashing damage; +2 melee damage with Strength attacks. Ends early if unable to attack or take damage.
At the first attack on your turn, gain advantage on Strength melee attacks; attacks against you have advantage until your next turn.
Advantage on Dexterity saving throws against effects you can see while not blinded, deafened, or incapacitated.

Once per short rest, identify a defensible route, high ground, or escape line. You and up to four allies gain advantage on the next group Survival or Investigation check made to navigate, escape, or set a watch.

Reaction, 2/short rest. When an ally within 10 feet is hit, move up to 10 feet toward them without provoking opportunity attacks. If adjacent after moving, reduce the damage by 1d6 + your Constitution modifier.

When you reduce a creature to 0 HP with a melee attack, you may knock it unconscious instead. Against a fleeing target, you may declare a leg-targeting strike; on a hit, deal normal damage and reduce speed by 10 feet until the end of its next turn.
A practical two-handed battleaxe carried by Toad Lee. Melee Weapon Attack: Strength; 1d10 slashing, versatile 1d12. Use the nonlethal pursuit option when the objective is capture, not execution.
Tough layered field leathers, scavenged and repaired by survivors. AC 14 + Dexterity modifier (max 2).
Rope, chalk, ration tin, bandages, whetstone, hooded lantern, oil, a hand-drawn route ledger, and a roll-call slate.
Proof of responsibility to the Wardens. It is not a badge of rank over survivors; it is a reminder that someone must answer the watch bell.
A field note recording the pursuit of Waluigi: target legs, not vital areas; secure the papers; account for thrown eyes and damaged flooring.
Level 4 advancement: +2 Strength (already reflected in the ability score).
